source_text: Dehinc manus imponitur, per benedictionem advocans et invitans Spiritum sanctum. Sane humano ingenio licebit spiritum in aquam arcessere et concorporationem eorum, accommodatis desuper manibus, alio spiritu tantae claritatis animare; Deo autem in suo organo non licebit per manus sanctas sublimitatem modulari spiritalem? Sed est hoc quoque de veteri sacramento, quo nepotes suos ex Joseph Ephraim et Manassem Jacob, capitibus impositis et intermutatis manibus, benedixerit, et quidem ita transversim obliquatis in se, ut Christum deformantes, jam tunc portenderent benedictionem in Christum futuram. Tunc ille sanctissimus Spiritus super emundata et benedicta corpora libens a Patre descendit, super Baptismi aquas, tanquam pristinam sedem recognoscens, conquiescit, columbae figura delapsus in Dominum, ut natura Spiritus sancti declararetur per animal simplicitatis et innocentiae, quod etiam corporaliter ipso felle careat columba. Ideoque: Estote, inquit, simplices sicut columbae, ne hoc quidem sine argumento praecedentis figurae. Quemadmodum enim post aquas diluvii, quibus iniquitas antiqua purgata est, post Baptismum (ut ita dixerim) mundi pacem coelestis irae praeco columba terris adnuntiavit dimissa ex arca, et cum olea reversa; quod signum etiam apud nationes paci praetenditur: eadem dispositione spiritalis effectus terrae, id est carni nostrae emergenti de lavacro post vetera delicta, columba sancti Spiritus advolat, pacem Dei afferens, emissa de coelis, ubi Ecclesia est arca figurata. Sed mundus rursus delinquit, quo male comparetur Baptismus diluvio. Itaque igni destinatur, sicut et homo qui post Baptismum delicta restaurat, ut hoc quoque in signum admonitionis nostrae debeat accipi.
pass_a_gloss: Then the hand is laid on, through blessing calling and inviting the Holy Spirit. Indeed, it will be permitted to human ingenuity to summon the spirit into the water and their incorporation, with hands accommodated from above, to animate with another spirit of such great clarity; but to God in His own instrument will it not be permitted through holy hands to modulate spiritual sublimity? But this is also from the old sacrament, by which Jacob blessed his grandchildren from Joseph, Ephraim and Manasseh, with hands imposed on their heads and interchangeably, and indeed in such a way transversely and obliquely in themselves, deforming Christ, already then portending the future blessing in Christ. Then that most holy Spirit willingly descends from the Father over the purified and blessed bodies, over the waters of Baptism, as if recognizing His former seat, rests, having fallen in the figure of a dove into the Lord, so that the nature of the Holy Spirit might be declared through the animal of simplicity and innocence, which dove also corporally lacks bile. And therefore: Be, He says, simple as doves, not even this without argument of the preceding figure. For just as after the waters of the flood, by which ancient iniquity was purified, after Baptism (so to speak) the dove, a herald of celestial wrath, announced peace to the earth, dismissed from the ark, and with an olive branch returned; which sign is also held out to the nations for peace: by the same disposition the spiritual effect on the earth, that is, on our flesh emerging from the bath after former sins, the dove of the Holy Spirit flies, bringing the peace of God, sent from heaven, where the Church is the figured ark. But the world again sins, by which Baptism is poorly compared to the flood. And so it is destined for fire, just as also the man who after Baptism restores sins, so that this also ought to be accepted as a sign of our admonition.

pass_b_english: Then the hand is laid on, through blessing calling and inviting the Holy Spirit. Indeed, human ingenuity is permitted to summon the spirit into the water and animate their incorporation with another spirit of such great clarity, with hands accommodated from above; but will it not be permitted to God in His own instrument to modulate spiritual sublimity through holy hands? Then that most holy Spirit willingly descends from the Father over the purified and blessed bodies, over the waters of Baptism, as if recognizing His former seat, rests, having fallen in the figure of a dove into the Lord, so that the nature of the Holy Spirit might be declared through the animal of simplicity and innocence, which dove also corporally lacks bile. But the world again sins, by which Baptism is poorly compared to the flood. And so it is destined for fire, just as also the man who after Baptism restores sins, so that this also ought to be accepted as a sign of our admonition.
